title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 18
statement: How many different remainders can result when the \(100\)th power of an integer is divided by \(125?\)

solutions.text: Here \(125 = 5^3\) and \(\varphi(125) = 100.\) If \(\gcd(n, 5) = 1,\) Euler’s theorem gives \(n^{100} \equiv 1 \pmod{125}.\) And if \(n\) is divisible by \(5,\) then \(n^{100}\) carries a factor of \(5^{100},\) hence of \(125,\) so \(n^{100} \equiv 0 \pmod{125}.\) That leaves only two possible remainders, \(0\) and \(1.\) Therefore, the answer is B.
hints: \(125 = 5^3\) and \(\varphi(125) = 100;\) split into \(n\) coprime to \(5\) and \(n\) divisible by \(5\)
If \(\gcd(n, 5) = 1,\) then \(n^{100} \equiv 1;\) if \(n\) is divisible by \(5,\) then \(n^{100}\) is divisible by \(5^3\)
